method: OPEN AND QUOTED from University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand' (April 2025). claims.claim: **Screen on the routine newborn dried blood spot, targeting absence of SMN1 exon 7.** (Evidence-based; strong)
claims.source_text: We recommend that newborn screening for SMA should be performed on the routine newborn dried blood spot with absence of exon 7 on SMN1 as the target analyte. Grade of recommendation Strong, for
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The screening method should have a sensitivity of at least 95% for 0 SMN1 copies.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: The screening method selected by the screening program should have a sensitivity of ≥ 95% for the detection of SMN1 exon 7 absence (0 SMN1 copies)
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Report a screen-positive SMN1 result to clinical services as soon as it is available, without waiting for SMN2 copy number.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: A screen positive result should be communicated to clinical services when the SMN1 screening result is available (independent of the availability of SMN2 copy number on
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure SMN2 copy number quickly, ideally within the screening process, but never let it delay notification of absent SMN1 exon 7.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: SMN2 copy number should be performed expeditiously, ideally as part of newborn screening processes using suitably validated quantitative assays but the result should not delay notification of the absence of exon 7 on SMN1.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SMN2 copy number is the main predictor of severity:** more copies generally mean a milder, later-onset phenotype. It is a guide, not absolute, because genotype and phenotype can be discordant.
claims.source_text: SMN2 copy number is the leading prognosticator of SMA disease severity, with higher copy numbers generally modifying phenotype to confer a milder phenotype and later clinical onset. … However, SMN2 copy number is a prognostic marker which is not absolute, and whilst it can act as a guide to management, discordant genotype-phenotype cases
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infants with 2 SMN2 copies are at highest risk of early onset:** up to 47% of screen-positive newborns with 2 copies show signs of SMA within the first month.
claims.source_text: newborns screening positive for SMA up to 47% of with those with 2 SMN2 copies, clinically display signs and symptoms of SMA onset within the first month of life.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screening programs should notify a screen-positive result to a paediatric neurologist and a local practitioner at the same time.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Newborn screening programs should establish a clinical referral pathway that includes simultaneous notification of a screen positive result to a paediatric neurology specialist and a
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis requires confirmed absence of SMN1 exon 7 (zero SMN1 copies).** (Evidence-based; strong)
claims.source_text: Diagnostic testing should include confirmation of an absence of exon 7 on SMN1 (i.e. zero copies of SMN1). Grade of recommendation: Strong, for
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnostic testing (whole blood, or a repeat dried blood spot from the recalled infant) should include SMN2 copy number** to predict severity and guide treatment decisions. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Diagnostic testing using suitably validated assays, from whole blood samples or repeat dried blood spot from a recalled infant should include SMN2 copy number as a guide to prediction of clinical severity and to facilitate therapeutic decision making.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Timelines:** diagnostic SMN1 results within 7 days at most of the lab receiving the sample; the full diagnosis (SMN1 and SMN2) within 30 days of birth, so treatment is not delayed. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Diagnostic results for SMN1 should be available as quickly as possible, and at maximum of 7 days of receipt of the sample by the diagnostic laboratory. … A diagnosis of SMA (including SMN1 and SMN2 copy number results) should be available to clinical services as quickly as possible. This should be completed within 30 days of birth to
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At the diagnostic visit, do immediately:** a neurological examination, venous blood for SMN1 exon 7, and venous blood (or a repeat dried blood spot) for SMN2 copy number. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: The following assessments should be completed immediately as part of the diagnostic and clinical evaluation of the newborn, who screens positive for SMA. … Neurological examination. … Venous sampling for quantification of SMN1 exon 7 on whole blood. • Venous sampling for determination of SMN2 copy number on whole blood OR repeat dried blood spot for confirmation of SMN2 copy number.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **False positive, false negative or uncertain results:** hold a joint case review across screening, diagnostic and clinical services and explain the findings to the family; if screening and diagnostic copy numbers differ, consider retesting by another method or laboratory. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: For newborns with a false positive, false negative or uncertain screening result, a case review with communication and collaboration between screening, diagnostic and clinical services should be conducted to understand the aetiology of results and explained to families. … If there is a difference in SMN1 and/or SMN2 copy number results between screening and diagnostic assays, retesting for SMN1 and/or SMN2 copy number with another method/laboratory should be considered.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If the diagnosis stays uncertain, a paediatric neurologist should follow the child until it is certain.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: If there is uncertainty as to the diagnosis of SMA the child should be clinically followed up by a paediatric neurologist until diagnostic certainty is reached.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Disclose a screen-positive result to the family within 2 working days of notification, and offer paediatric neurology or neuromuscular review within 2 working days of disclosure.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Screen positive result should be disclosed to the family within ≤ 2 working days (of notification to healthcare services). … Screen positive newborns should be offered a clinical review within paediatric neurology/neuromuscular services within ≤ 2 working days, from the time of screen positive disclosure.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A paediatric neurologist should disclose the diagnosis once SMN1 confirmation arrives, even if the SMN2 result is not yet back.** (Consensus)
claims.source_text: The process of disclosing a diagnosis of SMA to families should occur with a paediatric neurologist when SMN1 (diagnostic) confirmation is received, regardless of the availability of SMN2 copy number result.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Provide culturally safe care to Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, Pacific Islander, Māori and CALD families,** using a professional interpreter where the practitioner is not bilingual and Indigenous Health Liaison support where appropriate; direct families to reliable, nationally consistent resources. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Culturally safe care is required by healthcare practitioners when disclosing screening results to families from Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, Pacific Islander, Māori or other culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. If the healthcare practitioner is not bilingual, a professional interpreter should be used and advice and support sought from Indigenous Health Liaison professionals (which may include a First Nations nurse, midwife or healthcare practitioner) where relevant and appropriate. … Families receiving a diagnosis of SMA for their newborn through a newborn screening program, should be directed to high quality and reliable educational resources that reflect the contemporary care landscape and are nationally consistent.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Available SMN-augmenting treatments:** nusinersen and risdiplam (SMN2 splice modifiers) and onasemnogene abeparvovec (SMN1 gene transfer by viral vector). They support surviving motor units but cannot restore ones already irreversibly lost.
claims.source_text: Treatments have concentrated on SMN repletion or augmentation through inclusion of exon 7 in SMN2 through splice modification (to more reliably produce full-length pre-mRNA transcripts), leading to increase in stable SMN protein (nusinersen and risdiplam) or introducing SMN transgene into all cells within a viral vector (onasemnogene abeparvovecxioi). As such these treatments sit under the umbrella term of SMN augmenting or disease modifying therapies. For the purposes of the Guideline, the former definition is used in forming the recommendations. Whilst these treatments can help to support surviving lower motor neurons and the muscle fibres that they innervate (together known as a motor unit), they cannot replace irreversibly damaged motor units.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Symptomatic screen-positive newborns:** a paediatric neurologist should discuss immediate SMN-augmenting treatment with the family. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: For screen positive newborns who demonstrate signs and symptoms of SMA (consistent with disease onset i.e. clinically manifest), a paediatric neurologist should discuss options for immediate treatment with SMN augmenting treatments, with the family.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Presymptomatic newborns with 1, 2 or 3 SMN2 copies:** a paediatric neurologist should discuss immediate SMN-augmenting treatment with the family. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: For newborns with diagnostic confirmation of SMA and 1, 2 or 3 SMN2 copies and who are presymptomatic (i.e. clinically silent), a paediatric neurologist should discuss options for immediate SMN augmenting treatments, with the family.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start with a single agent (monotherapy), in a paediatric neurology treatment centre,** since there are no comparative data. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: In the absence of comparative data, single agent treatment i.e. monotherapy at initiation of therapeutic intervention is recommended, started within paediatric neurology treatment
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **4 or more SMN2 copies is the grey zone:** international advice ranges from immediate treatment to watching for symptoms, and access to treatment varies between countries.
claims.source_text: Treatment recommendations for infants with 4 SMN2 copies are evolving, with some guidelines advocating immediate treatment whilst others are in favour of a surveillance approach for symptom onset. (170-173), with access to SMN augmenting therapies in these individuals varying between countries.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Untreated infants** (no access to approved and reimbursed treatment, or the family chooses to wait) need review at least every 3 months for the first two years after diagnosis, then at least every 6 months. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Newborns with diagnostic confirmation of SMA who are unable to access approved and reimbursed treatments or chose not to be treated immediately, should have clinical follow-up with a minimum of 3 monthly assessments for the first two years from diagnosis, and minimum 6-monthly thereafter.
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer the family genetic counselling and cascade testing,** which may include referral to clinical genetics. (Consensus)
claims.source_text: Families of newborns diagnosed with SMA through newborn screening programs should be offered referral to, and review for genetic counselling and cascade testing (which may include referral to clinical genetics services).
claims.locator: University of New South Wales (Kariyawasam D and the Guideline Development Group); recommendations approved by the NHMRC CEO on 22 April 2025, 'Recommendations for Newborn Screening in Spinal Muscular Atrophy in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand', April 2025, https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/clinical-medicine/research-reports/nbs-for-sma/2025-07-nbs-sma-guideline.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
